intent: The button that opens and closes the panel of the Collapsible around it.
typical_uses: The always-visible caption a user presses to show or hide its Collapsible's panel

dont_use_when.situation: A standalone action with no panel to show or hide
A button that stays pressed or unpressed with no panel behind it

invariants.text: A disabled CollapsibleTrigger stays focusable and reports `aria-disabled` instead of taking the native `disabled` attribute, and ignores clicks, Enter and Space. Its own `disabled` replaces the root's for this trigger, so `disabled={false}` re-enables it under a disabled root.
The trigger carries `data-panel-open` while its panel is open and draws no open/closed indicator of its own; an icon a caller adds to show the state is styled off that attribute.

anti_patterns.dont: Put a Button inside a CollapsibleTrigger
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the trigger its caption directly - it already renders a native button, and a button inside a button is invalid HTML

a11y.by: The primitive's Collapsible.Trigger renders a native button with `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls` naming the panel's id; collapsible.test.tsx asserts the trigger is found by role button under its caption and that a click on a disabled one leaves the panel closed

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through collapsible.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A trigger with no Collapsible around it
bad.why: CollapsibleTrigger reads the nearest Collapsible's state through Base UI context and throws when there is none, so it cannot render on its own.

bad.title: A non-button element rendered without turning off nativeButton
bad.why: `nativeButton` stays true, so Base UI adds no button role or keyboard handling to the span and logs an error in development. Pass `nativeButton={false}` with a non-button element, or keep the default button.
